title: Enhancing Quantum Machine Learning with Anyons
authors: Da Zhang, Wen-Qiang Liu, Zhaohui Wei, Zhang-Qi Yin
abstract: The power of quantum computing and quantum machine learning relies on harnessing uniquely quantum phenomena as computational resources. While superposition, coherence and entanglement have been central to this effort, the role of particle exchange statistics remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce a quantum kernel framework that unifies bosonic, fermionic, and anyonic (fractional) exchange statistics within a single learning paradigm. We study this family of kernels from three perspectives. At the representation level, Haar-averaged effective-dimension analysis shows that fractional exchange phases access feature-space directions inaccessible to the purely symmetric or antisymmetric limits. At the level of kernel geometry, the corresponding Gram matrices show greater separation from the distinguishable-particle baseline and reduced label-dependent model complexity. Finally, on learning benchmarks, anyonic kernels consistently outperform their bosonic and fermionic counterparts, with stronger target alignment and more favorable class geometry. Together, these findings show that exchange statistics reshape the structure and geometry of quantum feature space, leading to enhanced learning performance. Our work identifies particle exchange statistics as an overlooked computational ingredient for quantum machine learning and provides the first systematic comparison of quantum learning models across exchange phases.
summary: This work introduces particle exchange statistics as a novel computational resource for Quantum Machine Learning. By constructing kernels that smoothly interpolate between bosonic and fermionic limits using photonic simulation, the authors show that intermediate 'anyon' statistics significantly enhance feature space geometry and classification accuracy over standard limits.
main_problem: To investigate whether particle exchange statistics can serve as an intrinsic, physical design principle for enhancing Quantum Machine Learning (QML).
main_result: Anyonic kernels consistently outperform their bosonic and fermionic counterparts on classification benchmarks, demonstrating that exchange statistics fundamentally reshape the quantum feature space structure.
method: The authors constructed a quantum kernel family interpolating between bosonic, fermionic, and anyonic statistics using photonic encoding. They analyzed this framework by calculating effective dimension, kernel geometry diagnostics, and direct machine learning performance.
model_or_system: The model uses an N-particle quantum feature state $|\Phi_\phi(\mathbf{x})angle$ derived from linear optical unitaries applied to entangled photons, where the exchange phase $\phi$ controls the statistics. This simulates fractional exchange behavior.
key_observables: Test accuracy on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST; Effective Dimension ($D_{	ext{eff}}(\phi)$); Geometric diagnostic ($gC_\phi$); Model complexity ratio ($R_\phi$).
important_parameters: Exchange Phase ($\phi$), which controls the statistics (Bosonic $\phi=0$, Fermionic $\phi=\pi$, Anyonic $0 < \phi < \pi$).
main_assumptions: The model simplifies physical anyons by reducing the braid structure to permutations, retaining only the exchange phase information.
figures_summary: Figures show that intermediate fractional phases maximize effective dimension and geometric separation. Test accuracy plots confirm peak performance at intermediate $\phi$, while KTA and inter-class distance diagnostics also favor these non-integer statistics.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the quantum kernel across different exchange phases ($\phi$). It first establishes the theoretical framework using particle state preparation, then quantifies the enhancement via feature space analysis (dimension/geometry), and finally validates the findings through supervised learning benchmarks.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete physical mechanism—particle statistics—to tune the representational power of quantum circuits for ML tasks, bridging fundamental condensed matter concepts (anyons) with applied quantum computation.
